How to use the Pomodoro timer

  1. Choose one task to work on, and put your phone away.
  2. Press Start and work until the chime: 25 minutes.
  3. Take the 5-minute break. The next round starts on its own.
  4. After four rounds, take the longer 15-minute break.

Use Full screen to hide everything else on the screen. To change the round lengths, the sound, the colours or switch to an analogue clock, use the timer settings.

What is the Pomodoro technique?

The Pomodoro technique is a way to study or work in short, focused blocks with planned breaks in between. Each block is called a “pomodoro”, after the tomato-shaped kitchen timer its inventor, Francesco Cirillo, used as a student. Short deadlines make it easier to start, and regular breaks keep you fresh for longer, which is why it works so well for homework, exam revision and long assignments.

Questions

How long is a Pomodoro?

The classic Pomodoro is 25 minutes of focused work followed by a 5-minute break. After four rounds you take a longer break of 15 to 30 minutes. This timer uses 25, 5 and 15 minutes, and you can change all three.

Is this Pomodoro timer free?

Yes. It is free to use, needs no account and has nothing to install. It runs in any modern browser on a computer, tablet or phone.

What happens if I refresh the page?

The timer remembers where it was, so refreshing the page or reopening the browser carries on from the same point.

Can I use it in class?

Yes. Open it full screen on the board or projector and the whole class can see how long is left in each round and break.
